item.title: COMING OCTOBER 7th | STRFKR w/ Happy Sad Face — Mon Sep 28 — Sierra Nevada Mills River
item.description: Wednesday, October 7 | Amphitheater Stage | 6 PM DOORS | 6:30PM SHOW | From $38.05 Event Details and Tickets Since forming in 2007, STRFKR have been perfecting a style that hides emotional complexities and existential searching in hyper-catchy, melody-forward pop music. The band’s spiritual and philosophical undercurrents never outshine their highly danceable sounds, but both are integral parts of what they do. Over the years and through the course of a discography that includes not just multiple studio albums but a wealth of fan-focused auxiliary releases, STRFKR’s combination of thoughtful lyricism and party starting hooks have made them a consistent success with critical music listeners and show-goers. item.title: Andrew Scotchie & Friends — Mon Sep 28, 6:00 PM — French Broad River Brewery
item.description: We’re SO excited to have Andrew Scotchie performing in the brewery again! It’s seriously awesome to b able to host this friend and local legend! Join singer-songwriter Andrew Scotchie as he brings in a singer-songwriter showcase on one Monday every month. Born and raised in Asheville, Andrew Scotchie is everything rock-n-roll was meant to be: sweaty, soul-stirring, a little dangerous, and absolutely alive. With the fire of the Stones, the blues of Lightnin’ Hopkins, and the message of a punk-fueled preacher, Scotchie and his all-star band have become a staple of the Southeast music scene . He’s shared stages with legends, crowd-surfed dive bars, and continues to craft his unique sound. His latest record, Love Is Enough, is a love letter to connection, chaos, and keeping your heart open in a world gone sideways. ​ Through consistent heartfelt releases, year round touring and active charity work, Asheville N.C. native Andrew Scotchie is a celebrated creative force. item.title: Monthly Dharma Group (Saturdays) – Meditation — Thu Oct 1, 10:30 PM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville You do not have to walk this path alone. In fact, this journey is that much more rich and enjoyable when traversed with others. Groups Openings
First Saturday of each month – mornings at 10:30 am Eastern Led by Buddhist teacher Ronya Banks, this group meets once a month, for an hour and a half.
Group Meeting Includes: Group Discussion and Sharing Instruction on Dharma/Buddhist Principles Guided Meditation Meditation Instruction Connecting with Other Practitioners Most people on a spiritual journey find it supportive, often even necessary to get the regular support of a meditation teacher, as well as the mutuality and connection with other meditation practitioners on this path.
This monthly group affords you with the opportunity to connect with a teacher and other like-minded people, wherein you will all boldly delve deeply into different ways of approaching your formal and informal mindfulness practices through the lens of the Buddhist teachings.
Price: By Donat

item.title: Tea & Tarot for the Collective — Sat Oct 3, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville Tarot readings are a powerful tool for tapping into the energies that surround us and exploring the depths of our psyche.
Experience an energetic vibe check as the cards illuminate pathways to understanding, clarity, and personal growth. We'll dive into the layers of our conscious, subconscious, and unconscious beings.
Marian will do a reading for the collective group first, then dive into mini-readings for each individual in attendance.
We will have local, organic, hot herbal tea from Appalachian DiviniTEA and water available to sip on during this event.
Suggested Exchange: $10
This event is hosted by Marian Noble of Energetic Experiences. She offers [private tarot readings](https://energeticexperiences.co/tarot) in person, online, and by phone.
Source: Awakening Asheville

item.title: Fun & easy way to play more tennis (please read event description for details) — Sat Oct 17, 7:00 PM
item.description:
PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis We’re still working to get more people into these Meetups, but our goal is to give PlayYourCourt members a few social tennis outings each week in addition to your practice sessions and Challenge League matches.
These Meetups are co-ed, super laid back, and all skill levels are welcome. Post your skill level and a suggested court in the comments section so we can round up as many players as we can for some tennis fun!
Also, if you’re looking to meet new practice partners or play some matches and you aren’t already in the PlayYourCourt Community, you can go here to see what we’re all about and sign up:
https://www.playyourcourt.com/tennis-community/asheville-nc/meetup/
If you love tennis, we’d love to have you! Be sure and watch the quick video that explains how everything works.
Happy hitting!
- Scott
Source: PlayYourCourt Asheville Tennis

item.title: Come sing with us! Vocal workshop and rehearsal - Land Of The Sky Chorus — Tue Oct 20, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Asheville Area A Cappella Singers Whether you are an experienced singer, or just like to sing in your car, come join us as our guest! The Land of The Sky Chorus, located in Asheville, NC, is welcoming guests - men and women - who are interested in joining us in the world-wide community of a cappella singing.
No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. Our repertoire of music is fun and spans many styles - most songs are easy to learn and sing. Learning materials are provided to help you get started, and you will be paired with a singing "Buddy" so you can join in right away.
We will be here to greet you as early as 6:15pm to help you get situated.
Source: Asheville Area A Cappella Singers

item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **TYPE OF HIKE:** Out & Back **DISTANCE:** 13.0 miles **ELEVATION GAIN:** approximately 3,250'
HIKE DESCRIPTION: Let’s enjoy one of the last few warm days of the season!!
This is a beautiful and challenging (level 10) roller-coaster style fitness hike on a well-maintained trail that trecks over several ridge lines to the Summit of Big Bald Mountain & back. This includes an initial climb to a grassy meadow from which one can see the summit of Big Bald, (the tallest peak centered in the picture). This trail then continues an up-and-down course along the NC and TN boundaries. There are at least 1 or 2 small springs that may be active at this time of the year. The summit is an open bald where we will break for a snack and enjoy the views before returning. The hike is mostly under a hardwood canopy until the summit. On the summit, the higher elevation temperatures are about 10 degrees cooler than Asheville's weather and often breezy.

item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.
